questions.stem: What does the abbreviation DLP stand for?
questions.explanation: DLP stands for Data Loss Protection/Prevention, part of an organisation's security strategy.

questions.stem: Which department normally handles and maintains DLP in an organisation?
questions.explanation: DLP is normally handled and maintained by the Risk department, where standards and policies are followed to protect data from intruders.

questions.stem: According to the DLP discussion, where do all standards and policies start from?
questions.explanation: The starting point of all standards and policies is the regulatory bodies.

questions.stem: At what moment does DLP come into action?
options: When a database is first created
When an employee joins the organisation
When data is archived to long-term storage
The moment data is exposed to outsiders via the Internet
questions.explanation: The moment you expose your data to outsiders via the Internet, DLP comes into action.

questions.stem: What is the stated purpose of DLP?
options: To increase the speed of data transfers
To improve the quality and consistency of data
To catalogue every dataset in the organisation
To reduce the cost of data storage
To protect or prevent data from getting into the wrong hands
questions.explanation: DLP is to protect or prevent data from getting into the wrong hands.

questions.stem: How has an organisation's choice about connecting to the external world changed in the DLP context?
options: In the previous era organisations could choose whether to connect; now there is no choice, they must connect to social media, the cloud and so on
In the previous era connection was mandatory; now organisations may stay fully isolated
Nothing has changed: connection has always been optional
Organisations may now connect only through their Risk department
Connection is now permitted only after regulatory approval
questions.explanation: In the previous era organisations had the choice to connect to the external world or not; now there is no choice, since they must connect to social media to pull data, connect to the cloud and so on.

questions.stem: Of what is DLP described as being a part?
questions.explanation: DLP is part of the organisational-level security strategy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT stated about DLP?
options: It is maintained by the Risk department
It follows standards and policies to protect data from intruders
It is triggered only when data stays entirely inside the organisation
Its purpose is to keep data out of the wrong hands
It becomes relevant once data is exposed via the Internet
questions.explanation: DLP comes into action the moment data is exposed to outsiders via the Internet, not when it stays entirely inside the organisation. The other statements are all made about DLP.

questions.stem: From whom must an organisation take care of its own data, according to the DLP discussion?
questions.explanation: One must take care of one's own data from intruders and hackers.

questions.stem: Which examples are given of external connections an organisation must now make, bringing DLP into play?
options: Connecting to a printer and a local file server
Connecting to an internal data warehouse and a reporting tool
Connecting to a regulator's portal and an audit system
Connecting to a payroll system and an HR database
Connecting to social media to pull data and connecting to the cloud
questions.explanation: Organisations must now connect to social media to pull data and must connect to the cloud, among other external connections.
